episodes.178881: Afternoon thunderstorms developed along a sharpening dryline across eastern NM. Storms strengthened as they tracked eastward toward the Texas border, producing large hail and even a landspout tornado. Hail reports ranged in size from pennies to golf balls and were focused across Quay and Curry counties. The landspout was reported just south of Texico and caused no damage.
episodes.179155: An isolated severe thunderstorm moved from north to|south across a portion of Southeast Texas on Tuesday, May 23. The|storm produced several reports of damage from multiple locations|between Huntsville and Conroe along the storm`s path through|Walker and Montgomery counties. One of the reports came from a|home construction site, where two people were reported killed and|seven injured when the home under construction collapsed.
episodes.179296: Thunderstorms with heavy rain and gusty winds developed over the area.  A few reports of trees down were received, and rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches resulted in reports of minor flooding.
episodes.179352: Another afternoon of severe thunderstorms occurred across the region on the 22nd. Severe thunderstorms dropped hail as large as two inches in diameter in several locations. The widespread thunderstorm activity organized into a larger complex of thunderstorms that produced heavy rain and severe wind gusts as it accelerated southeastward through the Rolling Plains during the evening. The bowing line of thunderstorms generated a peak wind gust of 80 mph as it moved across the Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site near Aspermont (Stonewall County). These severe winds also caused minor damage in and around Aspermont.
episodes.179484: Another consecutive evening of severe storms occurred on the Caprock on the evening of the 23rd as the atmosphere again became very unstable. Several of the thunderstorms were able to gain significant mid-level rotation which allowed them to generate very large hail. Hailstones as large as baseballs damaged multiple vehicles northwest of Shallowater (Lubbock County) along US Highway 84, while many other spots incurred impacts from hail as large as golf ball size. In addition to producing large hail, the slow moving storms also dumped torrential rainfall. One such pocket of torrential rain occurred just to the north of Plainview (Hale County), where several roads were underwater. Activity then shifted into the Rolling Plains late in the evening as activity morphed into upscale clusters of storms producing a few severe wind gusts.
episodes.180071: Severe storms affected eastern North Dakota, with a few isolated wind gusts and hail around quarter sized.
episodes.180260: Thunderstorms produced gusty outflow winds across SW Elko County.
episodes.180280: A front stalled across the local forecast area and served as a focus for localized heavy rainfall in diurnally enhanced sea breeze convection.
episodes.180317: Sea breeze convergence lead to showers and thunderstorms across southeastern Florida, on May 23rd. One of these produced a funnel cloud observed by the public.
episodes.180500: The Florida Keys remained in a weak pressure pattern between low pressure to the northeast of the Bahamas and high pressure over the central Gulf of Mexico.  Ample moisture was present for the development of isolated convective cells, including one waterspout.
episodes.180548: Abnormal late-May moisture and weak instability fueled scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Flash flooding and isolated severe weather occurred.
episodes.180679: A pattern developed by late May with sufficient moisture and forcing to yield scattered showers and thunderstorms almost every day, generally from the afternoon on into the early evening hours. Some of these storms were strong, yielding damaging wind gusts and hail. Additionally, a road washout was reported as a result of continued spring runoff from the prior winter's record snowfall.
episodes.180790: Early in the afternoon on the 22nd, multiple storms developed across the south central to southeastern Texas Panhandle. Some of these storms produced hail up to 1.5 and some heavy rainfall causing flooding in Gray County. Later in the afternoon a supercell developed over Beaver County in the Oklahoma Panhandle with another supercell forming in southwest Kansas before moving into the central and eastern portions of the Oklahoma Panhandle. These storms were in a very good environment for hail growth leading to reports of 2.5 diameter hail, especially once they got into Ochilltree County in the Texas Panhandle as they moved south to southeast. Some flooding was reported in Beaver County as well due to the initial storm then the Kansas storm training over the same area with heavy rainfall rates.
episodes.180791: Early in the afternoon on the 22nd, multiple storms developed across the south central to southeastern Texas Panhandle. Some of these storms produced hail up to 1.5 and some heavy rainfall causing flooding in Gray County. Later in the afternoon a supercell developed over Beaver County in the Oklahoma Panhandle with another supercell forming in southwest Kansas before moving into the central and eastern portions of the Oklahoma Panhandle. These storms were in a very good environment for hail growth leading to reports of 2.5 diameter hail, especially once they got into Ochilltree County in the Texas Panhandle. Some flooding was reported in Beaver County as well due to the initial storm then the Kansas storm training over the same area with heavy rainfall rates.
episodes.180868: The active weather pattern continued across the southern Great Plains. An active sub-tropical jet stream with embedded disturbances helped initiate thunderstorms off the higher elevations and along a dryline across the region. A few supercells produced large hail and damaging winds across the Permian Basin. A brief landspout was also reported with one thunderstorm.
episodes.180876: Thunderstorms formed in northwesterly flow aloft along a stationary boundary in Central Texas. Some of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.181148: Strong storms developed across the western Florida panhandle during the afternoon and produced large hail.
episodes.181188: Melting of record to near-record snowpack brought a period of flooding along the Salt River in Star Valley.
episodes.181363: Widespread severe weather with strong winds, large hail, and very heavy rains occurred on the 23rd in the Snake River Plain.
